focal_claim_designation.rationale: The article states two hypotheses. H1 (C01) is the primary claim and is operationalized by the HRM practice coefficients in the simultaneous-entry models (Table 3 models 2 and 3 for perceived organizational performance; Table 4 models 7 and 8 for perceived market performance), which the authors treat as the appropriate test because single-practice models (model 1/6) 'overstate the effects' (D1 p15). The practice-specific claims C02-C08 decompose C01 into the coefficients the authors themselves name as significant (training, incentive compensation, vertical hierarchy for Table 3; staffing selectivity, training, incentive compensation for Table 4; discussion D1 p18 names 'selectivity in staffing, training, and incentive compensation'). H2 (C13) is a stated hypothesis tested by models 4-5 and 9-10 and is retained as focal but secondary because the authors label it exploratory and conclude it is unsupported.
focal_claim_designation.aggregation_rule_proposal: Primary unit of evaluation: the seven HRM coefficients in Table 3 models 2 and 3 (full sample, perceived organizational performance), then the seven in Table 4 models 7 and 8. For each coefficient, score sign agreement and agreement of the one-tailed significance category (p<.01, p<.05, p<.10, n.s.) with the printed star level; treat the three practices the authors name as significant per outcome as the decisive subset. H1 overall is reproduced if (a) the HRM block joint F-test (Delta R2 F, footnote c) is significant at p<.05 for the model and (b) at least the same practices named by the authors are positive and significant at p<.10 one-tailed. H2 is reproduced if the interaction-block joint F-tests (footnote d) are non-significant and no interaction except training x staffing in model 5 reaches p<.10. Model 1/6 single-practice coefficients and the control coefficients are reported but weighted as secondary; descriptive targets (Tables 1-2) are diagnostics only. Where Table 3 and Table 4 conflict, Table 3 (larger sample, both sectors) governs the H1 verdict.
